result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-040-schema.md, closing docs/agents/design/REQ-040.md Sec3/Sec8 open question 3's deferral to DATA-DESIGNER (new invite_list_entries table, plus the uniqueness/remove-mechanism decisions CODE-DESIGNER explicitly left open). Read REQ-040.md in full first, then apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts in full (confirmed no invite_list_entries table exists; confirmed audit_log.entity_id carries NO foreign key -- uuid().notNull() with no .references() call, REQ-011.md Sec7's polymorphic-column design -- load-bearing for the hard-delete decision below; confirmed every existing person/entity FK in this schema is ON DELETE RESTRICT uniformly, no CASCADE/SET NULL anywhere), apps/bot/drizzle/meta/_journal.json (latest 0007_sturdy_network, this table's migration expected as 0008_*), decisions/0005-orm-drizzle.md (Drizzle-generated migration convention, unchanged), and REQ-031-schema.md/REQ-032-schema.md as this role's own precedent for column-table format, migration prose, and open-question restraint.

Column shape (Sec1): id uuid PK; event_id uuid NOT NULL FK->events.id RESTRICT; user_id uuid NOT NULL FK->users.id RESTRICT; invite_code_id uuid NULLABLE FK->invite_codes.id RESTRICT (an entry can exist before any code is issued, per STORY-DETAILS F9 step 2, unchanged from REQ-040.md); added_by uuid NOT NULL FK->users.id RESTRICT; opened_at timestamptz NULLABLE (REQ-040.md Sec3.2's semantics reused unchanged, not revisited); name text NOT NULL (handler-level blank-refusal, REQ-040.md Sec4.1, also enforced at the row level -- same belt-and-suspenders discipline chk_registrations_checked_in_only_if_admitted/chk_feedback_nps_range already establish); company/position text NULLABLE, no default (createWalkinProfile's established '' -> null convention, application-level translation, not schema-level); created_at/updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(). DECISION: no separate added_at column -- REQ-040.md Sec3.1 left open whether it duplicates created_at; resolved that it does, so created_at alone serves that role (Sec1.1 -- this table has no update-in-place history that would make the two diverge, unlike registrations' created_at vs admission-decision-time).

Uniqueness (Sec2): ADOPTED UNIQUE(event_id, user_id) as a plain (non-partial) unique index, uq_invite_list_entries_event_user, mirroring registrations'/event_staff's own identical membership-table precedent. Not partial, because remove is a hard delete (below) so no soft-state column exists for a partial index to exclude.

Remove mechanism (Sec3): HARD DELETE, not removed_at. Directly answers the handoff's own question -- confirmed audit_log.entity_id has no FK, so a hard DELETE does not break AC11's 'exactly one audit_log row' requirement; the row order (write audit before/with the DELETE, same transaction) is BACKEND-DEV's implementation detail, not a schema constraint. Reasoned on the merits (Sec3.2): no AC/story asks for a removed entry to stay visible or reactivatable; a removed_at marker would force UNIQUE(event_id,user_id) to become a partial index purely to route around a self-inflicted re-add conflict, for no real query benefit; this table records membership (binary), not an outcome needing history the way registrations.admission does -- audit_log's own add/remove rows already carry that history. This also resolves REQ-040.md Sec8 open question 4 (re-adding a previously removed guest) as a non-issue: DELETE then a fresh INSERT, no special-case rule needed.

Relink-under-uniqueness trace (Sec4, the handoff's most load-bearing ask): confirmed a real conflict risk exists -- if the redeemer's own existing account B already has its own invite_list_entries row for an event A also has an entry for (via REQ-040.md Sec2.4's all-of-A's-events repoint scope), UPDATE user_id=B WHERE user_id=A would violate the new unique index for that one event. Traced a concrete two-row scenario (A has entries for E1+E2; B independently already has its own entry for E2) and resolved it with a two-statement, single-transaction sequence: (1) UPDATE ... WHERE user_id=A AND NOT EXISTS (a same-event row already under B) -- repoints every non-conflicting entry; (2) DELETE WHERE user_id=A -- removes whatever conflicting rows step 1's WHERE clause skipped, since B's own pre-existing entry for that event is already the correct, more-authoritative row (an organizer's deliberate direct listing of the real person) and needs no data copied from A's superseded duplicate. Confirmed this composes cleanly with REQ-040.md Sec2.4 point 1's separate invite_codes.issued_to_user_id repoint (no analogous unique constraint on that column to collide with, per REQ-033.md's own open question 2). Extended REQ-040.md Sec2.4 point 4's audit-row count ('one row per repointed entry') to read as one row per entry A originally held, whether the outcome is an UPDATE or a DELETE -- flagged explicitly in Sec9 open question 2 as this artefact's own reading, not silently assumed, since REQ-040.md's own text did not enumerate this sub-case.

Business-card field placement (Sec1.3, weighing in on REQ-040.md Sec8 open question 1 from a data-design angle only -- the S1 consent-scope question itself remains SECURITY-REVIEWER's at Step 2c, not re-decided here): concurred the fields belong on invite_list_entries, adding three data-shape arguments beyond CODE-DESIGNER's consent-boundary reasoning -- no third 'guest' table is available per this requirement's own stated non-goal; the fields are more correctly per-entry than per-person (an organizer's business-card knowledge of a guest can legitimately differ across two separate event listings, e.g. a changed employer, without overwriting a shared value); Sec4.2's display-precedence COALESCE(profiles.x, entry.x) shape needs both sides to exist as genuinely separate columns. Confirmed name NOT NULL / company+position nullable directly answers the handoff's minimal-entry question: a name-only add is a legal row.

Migration (Sec7): additive only, expected as apps/bot/drizzle/0008_*.sql (CREATE TABLE plus the one unique index and four FK constraints), no ALTER of any existing table, fully reversible via a plain DROP TABLE with zero data loss elsewhere. No implementation code, no migration file, and no schema.ts edit performed by this artefact itself -- BACKEND-DEV's Step 2 responsibility, per decisions/0005 and this role's own mandate.

issues.description: REQ-040-schema.md Sec9 open question 1: the Sec1.3 data-design concurrence with REQ-040.md Sec3.4 is offered as support only, not a second vote overriding SECURITY-REVIEWER -- REQ-040.md Sec8 open question 1 (the S1 consent-scope boundary for organizer-known business-card data) remains open, routed to Step 2c exactly as CODE-DESIGNER left it. Not resolved by this artefact.

REQ-040-schema.md Sec9 open question 2: the relink-conflict audit-row-count reading (Sec4.3 -- one row per entry A originally held, covering both the UPDATE and DELETE outcomes) is this artefact's own extension of REQ-040.md Sec2.4 point 4's literal text to a sub-case that document did not itself enumerate. Flagged for CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR/SECURITY-REVIEWER to confirm explicitly rather than silently accepted.

REQ-040-schema.md Sec9 open question 3 (Sec5's anonymization row): whether a permanently-retired, entry-less placeholder users row (post-relink A) should be in scope for a future S13 anonymization routine is left open -- no such routine exists yet in this codebase to decide it against, same restraint REQ-031-schema.md/REQ-032-schema.md already exercised for their own tables.
